from collections import Counter

def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    fill = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row if v != 0).most_common(1)[0][0]

    # Repeated solid tiles have the greatest fill-color count in ordinary
    # rows/columns. Separator lines have fewer fill cells; this also catches
    # separator rows partly interrupted by encoded markers.
    row_fill = [sum(v == fill for v in row) for row in grid]
    col_fill = [sum(grid[r][c] == fill for r in range(h)) for c in range(w)]
    max_row, max_col = max(row_fill), max(col_fill)
    rlines = [r for r, n in enumerate(row_fill) if n < max_row]
    clines = [c for c, n in enumerate(col_fill) if n < max_col]

    if len(rlines) < 2 or len(clines) < 2:
        return [row[:] for row in grid]

    # The most frequent color where separator lines cross is their framework.
    framework = Counter(grid[r][c] for r in rlines for c in clines).most_common(1)[0][0]
    out = []
    for i in range(len(rlines) - 1):
        row = []
        for j in range(len(clines) - 1):
            corners = (grid[rlines[i]][clines[j]], grid[rlines[i]][clines[j + 1]],
                       grid[rlines[i + 1]][clines[j]], grid[rlines[i + 1]][clines[j + 1]])
            row.append(corners[0] if corners[0] != framework and len(set(corners)) == 1 else fill)
        out.append(row)

    # Remove unmarked outer margins, preserving empty cells within the figure.
    active = [(r, c) for r, row in enumerate(out) for c, value in enumerate(row) if value != fill]
    if not active:
        return [[fill]]
    r0, r1 = min(r for r, c in active), max(r for r, c in active)
    c0, c1 = min(c for r, c in active), max(c for r, c in active)
    return [row[c0:c1 + 1] for row in out[r0:r1 + 1]]
